title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 1 (Short title, extent and commencement)

content.overview: Section 1 provides that this Act may be called the Indian Contract Act, 1872. It extends to the whole of India and came into force on the first day of September, 1872. Nothing in the Act affects the provisions of any Statute, Act or Regulation not hereby expressly repealed, nor any usage or custom of trade, nor any incident of any contract, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.
content.glance: Short title; extent whole of India; commencement 1 Sept 1872; saving for unrepealed law, trade usage, consistent contract incidents.
content.study: The Act is titled the Indian Contract Act, 1872. It extends to the whole of India and commenced on 1 September 1872. A saving clause preserves unrepealed statutes, trade usage or custom, and incidents of any contract that are not inconsistent with the Act. Current-law framing: state short title, extent and commencement; apply the saving where a usage, custom or unrepealed statute is invoked.

sections.heading: Short title
sections.body: This Act may be called the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

sections.heading: Extent and commencement
sections.body: It extends to the whole of India and came into force on 1 September 1872.

sections.heading: Saving
sections.body: Nothing affects unrepealed Statutes/Acts/Regulations, usage or custom of trade, or any incident of a contract not inconsistent with this Act.

examples.title: Trade usage not inconsistent
examples.body: A trade usage consistent with the Act may still operate under the saving in section 1.

hypotheticals.question: Does the Act displace every trade custom?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 1 saves usage or custom of trade not inconsistent with the Act.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-1
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: The Contract Act overrides every trade usage.
misconceptions.correction: Section 1 expressly saves usage or custom of trade not inconsistent with the Act.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 1 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State short title, extent and commencement. II. Apply the saving if usage, unrepealed statute or contract incident is raised. III. Conclude.

examTips: Mention the saving for trade usage.
